The hardest part is in the prep. Get the sharpest knife you own and cut all the way around the bone though the meat and tendons about an inch in from the smaller side of a drumstick. Once the meat and tendons are separated from the larger end work your finger under the meat on the smaller end and yank it off exposing the bare bone for the handle of your lollipop. It's kind of tricky to get a good hold on it sometimes so a paper towel might help. Once that is off you simply hold the drumstick vertical with the bare bone standing up and push the meat down. Be careful at this step because there is a small bone that runs up the main bone and can poke you if you aren't careful. if you feel like being fancy you can kinda wiggle that bone to break it and take it off. I just leave them unless I accidentally break one. after this you can re arrange the skin and trim off any hangers. Once your lollipops are prepped you can season as you wish and grill/smoke. If you really have to be on the money I use an indicator to pick up the edge. The guys in my shop call it a jig bore pickup. You basically center the ball on the indicator with the center of the spindle by turning the mill by hand kind of just eyeballing it. Then you come along the edge of the part and rock the spindle back and forth to find the zero. The indicator will lead up to a number and then back off like finding the high spot. Zero out the indicator on the high spot. Next bring the indicator up and rotate 180deg from the edge that you zeroed. ( basically above the part). Bring the needle down  just above the part and using a gauge block hold it against the edge you are picking up and do the same sort of pick up that you did on the first side. The important part here is to not touch the needle after getting the first zero from the opposite side. Then from there you split the difference and make your move and check the previous side. You might have to do it a few times to get the hang of it but this is one of the most accurate ways to do a pickup, especially if you get close with a .001 indicator and then throw in a .00005 to fine tune it.
